div.div: The kernel owns the envelope; each experience owns only an opaque local story that runs inside the one shared phase 'in story', and cannot write anything around it
THE KERNEL ENVELOPE (kernel-owned; an experience reads it through a read-only view)

execution mode and lifecycle phase | deployment generation and session ID | provisional visitor candidate, active participant binding, reattach / departure / retirement state | capability health | visitor-audio permit (listening, per session) and speech-output lease (speaking, per turn), kept apart | action leases and per-invocation claims, open intervals, pending cancellations | timers, deadlines, pending commands | cleanup, safety, stop and recovery state | selected experience ID + revision | the opaque local state
LIFECYCLE PHASE - one closed set shared by every experience (listed in the order of note B2)
not ready
ready
selecting
in story
cleanup
safe cleanup
stopped
recovery
LOCAL STORY STATE - private to the selected experience, opaque to the kernel, valid only in 'in story'. Example: the wave experience, story greet -> await_wave -> wave (B1).

greet
(chapter)

await_wave
starts a 10 s gesture-wait timer [I1]

wave
(timer cancelled)

gesture_not_observed
(terminal local state)
Its only effect: 'request completion cleanup'. A visitor-gesture input from any OTHER track is rejected at admission and never reaches this reducer (B4).

RECOVERY is kernel-owned: unresolved claims stay in evidence and visitor admission stays off. Only explicit operator recovery, or a clean restart that proves the old authority cannot act, leaves it. The first coordinator treated this timeout as a clean stop; the kernel design corrects that (B2).

PARTICIPANT AUTHORITY - kernel
selects the candidate, ties a handshake to a track, authorises lock, retarget, reattach and departure, retires the participant, and passes the reducer a typed decision: provisional | locked | retargeted | reattached | departed.
Current participant track = active binding's track, else the candidate's; none before selection or after retirement. Invariant, independent of any story state: never a candidate AND an active participant.

PARTICIPANT POLICY - experience
only its story response plus typed options the kernel exposes, e.g. 'lock the participant when the handshake times out: yes / no'. A new lock rule or grace is a kernel change and a safety review.
AFTER EVERY REDUCTION, in order: 1 kernel invariants on the tentative envelope (cannot be waived) -> 2 story validator (reads the envelope view, cannot change it). A failure commits nothing.

LOCAL STATE CONTRACT: schema version | required state_name | deep immutability (scalars, enums, tuples, frozen records; no lists, maps, sets, callables) | one kernel-owned canonical encoding | equality = equal encodings. The simulation, browser and gateway may branch only on the kernel phase and on projector values, never on a local state name.

TWO LEVELS OF PROFILE: the experience PROFILE (content-addressed) pins target, images, config and ABI digests, accepted inputs and primitives, catalog policy, readiness, cleanup, evidence and acceptance, and exactly one definition. The DEFINITION selects only story logic, so a story never picks its own privileges.

Legend: amber = kernel-owned | green = experience-owned | red = recovery | blue = deployment profile | dashed amber frame = the envelope, dashed green frame = the opaque story inside 'in story'. Only the transitions the notes state are drawn between phases; the others are not.

Sources. Mechanisms: this kit's notes/ (named per line below) and glossary.md. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown: [Pn] = public (cited); [In] = illustrative (a round design parameter that keeps the design's relations; never a measurement of any system); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/B2-state-ownership.md (envelope fields, lifecycle phases, two validators, participant authority vs policy, current participant track, local state contract, cleanup failure to recovery, two profile levels); B1-experiences-as-reducers.md (the wave example); B4 (admission of participant-bound inputs). Public: Harel, 'Statecharts', Science of Computer Programming 8(3), 1987 (a story nested inside one lifecycle state).
[I1] gesture_wait_timeout_s_illustrative = 10 s. illustrative: design parameter; experience-policy timer for the 'await wave' local state of the example wave experience
[I2] cleanup_ack_timeout_ms_illustrative = 10 000 ms. illustrative: design parameter; kernel cleanup acknowledgement deadline. Every settle bound must be strictly shorter

gesture = wave from the
current participant track
cleanup deadline 10 000 ms [I2] passes without quiescence proof
